clue.text: Out of Scotland in small island part of Borneo

indicators.note: in places the Scottish word inside the island's name

parts.note: Sark is a small island among the Channel Islands
awa is the Scots form of away, i.e. out

explanation.surface: Someone is away from Scotland, staying on a little island somewhere in Borneo.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarawak is a Malaysian state occupying the north-western part of the island of Borneo.

clue.text: Star reported by poet with girl's name

indicators.note: reported means as spoken, so the poet's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet of The Faerie Queene
Tracy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A star is spoken of by a poet, along with a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Spencer Tracy was a Hollywood film star, the famous screen partner of Katharine Hepburn.

clue.text: Minor shiner to move fast with little weight

parts.note: to rush is to move fast
light means having little weight

explanation.surface: A small lamp darts about while weighing almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rushlight is a feeble candle made by dipping a rush in tallow, so a modest source of light.

clue.text: Picture of both coming out of me another way

indicators.note: coming out suggests the letters emerging in a new form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A film starring both of them emerges from me in a different manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture of both' means a film starring both 4 20 and 1 down 23 down; the letters of 'of me another way' are rearranged, with 'another way' supporting the idea of a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Woman of the Year (1942) was the first film pairing Katharine Hepburn with Spencer Tracy.

clue.text: Star could be a thinker with a switched-on stream

indicators.note: could be says these letters might form something else when rearranged

parts.note: hep is old slang for switched-on or hip
a burn is a Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: A star might be an intellectual with an electrified river.
explanation.definitionFit: Katharine Hepburn was a Hollywood film star who won four acting Oscars.

clue.text: Picture of 1 down 23 down without 4 20, in whom it's got what another went with

parts.note: taken as written
whom points to 4 20 herself, giving her
it's gives it
another film was Gone with the Wind, so it went with the wind

explanation.surface: A film starring Tracy alone, in which someone has what another film went with.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is IN HER (in whom, i.e. in Katharine Hepburn) + IT + THE WIND, from the film title Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Inherit the Wind (1960) starred Spencer Tracy but not Katharine Hepburn.

clue.text: Not mainstream with trendy end

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
to die is to come to an end

explanation.surface: Something alternative ends up as fashionable at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Indie describes music or films from independent producers, outside the commercial mainstream.

clue.text: Novel stream hid in novel

indicators.note: in novel means in a new fashion, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A book in which a river is concealed in a new way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' appears twice: first as the definition, then 'in novel' as the signal to rearrange 'stream hid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard Times is a novel by Charles Dickens set in an industrial town.

clue.text: Perch that may be ruled

definitions.meaning: from the idiom to rule the ..., meaning to be in charge

explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a bird's perch, and one who dominates is said to rule it.

clue.text: See 5 across
Letters to order of course

parts.note: Eps is short for epistles, letters of the New Testament
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Correspondence required, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally' but defines a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a famous English racecourse where the Derby is run.

clue.text: Hybrid from breeding establishment lost leader or rebelled

indicators.note: lost leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a stud is a farm for breeding horses
rose, as in rose up, means rebelled

explanation.surface: A crossbred animal from a stud farm, whether it lost its leader or rebelled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor rose combines the red rose of Lancaster and the white of York, a heraldic hybrid.

clue.text: Mountain pass entering valley in London

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountains
entering means going in
a dale is a valley

explanation.surface: A mountain pass leads into a valley somewhere in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Colindale is a district located in north London, in the borough of Barnet.

clue.text: "Everyone … singing" and starting saying it was wrong

indicators.note: starting means only the start of the word is used, its ending dropped

parts.note: tutting is clicking the tongue in disapproval, saying something was wrong

explanation.surface: All are singing, and someone begins to complain it was a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: TUTTING loses its final NG, leaving the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the musical direction for all performers to play or sing together.

clue.text: Accent has given away born villain

indicators.note: given away means a letter has been taken out

parts.note: a brogue is a regional accent, especially Irish

explanation.surface: Someone's accent betrays that they were born a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest scoundrel, a synonym for villain.

clue.text: Good chance entering cooked eels for snack

indicators.note: entering means going inside the other letters
cooked suggests the letters are prepared in a new order

parts.note: evens is a fifty-fifty betting chance, a good one

explanation.surface: A fair bet that cooked eels will make a light bite.
explanation.walkthrough: Evens, in betting, is an even-money chance, here called good; 'cooked' rearranges the eels around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack, eaten around eleven o'clock.

clue.text: Stop in pub for dinner first if having authority

indicators.note: in places the punctuation mark inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a comma is a punctuation stop

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of dinner

explanation.surface: Halting at a pub to eat first, if you are in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in command is to hold authority over others.

clue.text: Spanish town (28 one largely inapplicable)

indicators.note: largely means most of the word is kept, one letter dropped

parts.note: 28 is African, and the African city meant is Carthage
n/a is short for not applicable

explanation.surface: A Spanish town, an African one mostly irrelevant.
explanation.walkthrough: Cartagena was founded as New Carthage; CARTHAGE loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartagena is a port city in south-eastern Spain.

clue.text: Picture judge with joint problem, cold not hot

indicators.note: cold not hot means one letter takes the place of the other

parts.note: arthritic describes someone suffering joint disease
h is the abbreviation for hot on taps
c is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A judge of paintings has arthritis, feeling cold rather than hot.
explanation.definitionFit: An art critic judges paintings and other pictures professionally.

clue.text: See 3
Unconscious of taking the air in winter?

explanation.definitionFit: Out cold means fully unconscious, and literally describes someone out in cold weather.

clue.text: Screamer used the current hustings — the tops!

definitions.text: Screamer used the current hustings — the tops!

indicators.note: the tops means the first letters of the words

explanation.surface: The screaming politician made use of today's election platforms, and they were great.
explanation.walkthrough: Screaming Lord Sutch founded the Monster Raving Loony Party and stood in many British elections.
explanation.definitionFit: David Sutch styled himself Screaming Lord Sutch, a rock singer and fringe candidate.

clue.text: See 4
Headgear said to be used in Stoke-on-Trent

indicators.note: said signals a word that sounds the same
used in shows the letters sitting within the place name

parts.note: the letters TOKE run inside this place name

explanation.surface: A hat said to be worn in a Potteries city.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoke-on-Trent is an English city in the Potteries.
explanation.definitionFit: A toque is a small brimless hat, also a chef's tall white hat.

clue.text: See 28
Reprimand severely — must be detached

definitions.meaning: from the idiom tear a strip off someone
a packaging strip pulled away to open it

explanation.definitionFit: To tear a strip off is to scold, and a tear strip is pulled off to open a packet.

clue.text: See 1
Day on back line for butterfly or wolf

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday

indicators.note: back means the letters are read the other way

parts.note: Ry is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A day spent on the back line for a butterfly or wolf.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a type of brown butterfly and also a lecher, a wolf.

clue.text: Exaggerate situation of government?

definitions.meaning: the government stands above the nation

explanation.definitionFit: To overstate is to exaggerate, and government sits over the state.

clue.text: Officer must leave vegetable and turn to armadillo

indicators.note: must leave means those letters go away

parts.note: a potato is a vegetable
PO is a petty officer
U as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: An officer must abandon a vegetable and switch to an armadillo.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatou is a name for an armadillo, especially the giant armadillo.

clue.text: I abandon your handiwork for unpleasant series of 22s etc

indicators.note: abandon means the letter is dropped

parts.note: DIY is do-it-yourself, your own handiwork
nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: I give up home improvements for a nasty run of royals.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is QUEEN, so 22s etc are royal rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a line of hereditary rulers such as kings and queens.

clue.text: Picture of 4 20 without 1 down 23 down of Balkis?

definitions.meaning: a Hepburn film without Tracy, co-starring Bogart
Balkis is a name for the ... of Sheba, a ruler from Africa

explanation.definitionFit: The African Queen (1951) starred Hepburn with Humphrey Bogart; Balkis was a monarch from Africa.
